cases.question: What is COMP 4537 Internet Software Architecture about?
cases.standalone_question: What is COMP 4537 Internet Software Architecture about?
cases.answer_excerpt:
**COMP 4537 Internet Software Architecture** is a 3.0-credit course focused on the design, development, and management of web APIs. It teaches students how to build secure, well-documented, and functional backend API servers using RESTful architecture.

### Key Topics Covered
* **RESTful APIs:** Understanding what RESTful APIs are, why they matter, and how HTTP and REST APIs relate.
* **Core Operations & Constraints:** Working with CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) operations, REST constraints, and HTTP status codes.
* **Asynchronous Programming:** Developing for single-threaded environments using Node.js, modules, and Promises.
* **Security:** Implementing database security following the Principle of Least Privilege (PoLP), securing API services using HTTPonly cookies, Public/Private keys, JWT, SSL, oAuth, and Bearer Tokens.
* **Web Technologies:** Working with JSON, LocalStorage, AJAX, CORS, and the Express framework.

### Course Details
* **Prerequisites:** COMP 1537 and COMP 3522.
* **Program:** Part of the Computer Systems Technology (CST) Diploma (Full-time).
* **Evaluation:** 30% Midterm Exam, 30% Final Exam, 15% Quizzes, 10% Assignments, 10% Group Project, and 5% Class Participation. Both exams are held in-person on the Learning Hub, requiring students to bring their own laptops.

### Sources
* https://www.bcit.ca/courses/internet-software-architecture-comp-4537/
* https://www.bcit.ca/outlines/20261088086/
* https://www.bcit.ca/programs/computer-systems-technology-d

cases.question: What are the entrance requirements for the Computer Systems Technology diploma?
cases.standalone_question: What are the entrance requirements for the Computer Systems Technology diploma?
cases.answer_excerpt:
For the full-time Computer Systems Technology (CST) diploma, applicants must meet specific academic requirements. 

**Entrance Requirements:**
* **English:** English Language Proficiency Category 2 – English Studies 12 (67%) or equivalent.
* **Math:** Pre-Calculus 12 (67%) or equivalent.

**Application Process:**
* Applications are accepted on a first-qualified basis as long as space remains. 
* Applications open on October 1st for the Fall (September) intake and March 15th for the Winter (January) intake. 
* It is highly recommended to apply early and submit all supporting documents as PDF files.

**Direct Entry Option:**
If you have completed equivalent coursework at BCIT or another institution, you can apply for direct entry into level 2 or 3. To do this, you must email cstdiploma@bcit.ca for a pre-assessment kit and submit the approved assessment with your application. The deadlines for direct entry are July 15th for the Fall intake and November 30th for the Winter intake. Note that direct entry students are not eligible for the Co-op program.

Sources:

cases.question: Am I automatically enrolled in the BCITSA Health and Dental Plan, and can I opt out?
cases.standalone_question: Am I automatically enrolled in the BCITSA Health and Dental Plan, and can I opt out?
cases.answer_excerpt:
### BCITSA Health and Dental Plan Enrollment and Opt-Out

#### 1) Automatic Enrollment
Yes, you are automatically enrolled in the BCITSA Extended Health & Dental Plan if you meet the following criteria:
* You are registered in a BCIT program designated as full-time.
* Your program is at least 16 weeks in length.

If you meet these requirements, the Student Association (SA) Health fee of $294.00 per year is automatically included in your tuition upon registration. Students in ISEP or part-time/flexible learning programs are not eligible for automatic enrollment.

#### 2) Opt-Out Process
You can opt out of the plan if you already have comparable extended health and dental coverage (such as through a parent, spouse, or employer). 

* **How to opt out:** You must submit your opt-out request online. 
* **Deadline:** The opt-out deadline is strictly **30 days from the start of your program**. This process is done once every 12 months. After this 30-day deadline passes, opt-outs cannot be processed.

### Sources
* https://www.bcit.ca/admission/tuition-fees/full-time-studies/

For standard academic programs, newly admitted international students must pay a non-refundable commitment fee of **$6,000** to secure their seat and confirm acceptance. This fee is later applied to your tuition. 

However, if you are accepted into the English for Professional and Academic Success (EPAS) program, the non-refundable commitment fee is **$1,000**.

### 1) BCIT Peer Tutoring Cost and Fees
Yes, peer tutoring is completely free and available to all BCIT students. It is offered on a drop-in basis both in person and online, meaning no advance registration is required.

### 2) BCITSA Health and Dental Plan Opt-Out
Yes, you can opt out of the BCITSA Student Health and Dental Plan if you are already covered by comparable extended health and dental benefits. To do so, you must submit your opt-out request within 30 days from the start of your program. This deadline occurs once every 12 months, and opt-outs cannot be processed after this date.

### 3) BCIT Burnaby Campus Student Housing Residences
The Burnaby campus offers the following student housing options:
*   **Tall Timber Student Housing:** Opened in Fall 2025, this facility offers fully self-contained Studio rooms and Connected Single rooms.
*   **Legacy Townhouses:** These host 12 students each in private rooms with shared common facilities.

cases.question: Which English proficiency categories does BCIT use for admissions?

prior_turns.question: Which English proficiency categories does BCIT use for admissions?

cases.answer_excerpt:
For Category 2 English language proficiency, the required TOEFL iBT score depends on your program start date:

* **Prior to January 21, 2026:** You must achieve an overall score of 86, with no section score less than 20.
* **As of January 21, 2026:** You must achieve an overall score of 4.5, with individual section scores of at least 3.5 in Speaking, 3.5 in Writing, 3.5 in Reading, and 3.5 in Listening.

For these assessment tests, your results must be dated no more than two years before your program start date.
